brief: A system monitor where CPU/memory are organisms — healthy breathes steady, stressed pulses fast

dominant_strengths: Clean dark palette with well-tuned green/red glow that conveys state semantics instantly without legend
Crisp typographic hierarchy: bold metric numerals anchor each panel against quiet uppercase status labels
Symmetric split composition reads as a clear dual-organ dashboard at a glance
dominant_weaknesses: Organism metaphor is asserted but not visible — orbs look like static buttons, no breath/pulse rhythm cues in the still frame
PROC and MEM tokens feel placeholder-ish; they reduce 'organism' to generic dev labels and undercut the living-creature concept
Symmetric halo treatment for both healthy and critical states means red and green share identical geometry, weakening behavioral differentiation
fix_priorities: Differentiate organism morphology between states: irregular fast pulse for critical, slow even bloom for healthy, with visible motion trails in stills
Replace PROC/MEM tokens with heartbeat/waveform glyphs or live BPM-style rate indicator to make 'organism' literal
Add secondary telemetry (history sparkline, breath rate) so the panels reward closer reading beyond a single big number
rationale.norman_balance: Strong visceral glow and decent reflective metaphor, but behavioral layer is thin — nothing animates or invites interaction in the static composition.
rationale.intent_fit: Partially fits: color and glow imply life, but without depicted motion or rhythm cues the 'organism' brief stays conceptual rather than embodied.
